posts.author: firestalker
posts.body:
Short answer.... Yes, you can
This is my normal attack sequence:
<setup action>
display action
wait: 25
CLEAR BATTLE LOG
CAMERA FOCUS: user, CENTER, 75
ZOOM: 150%, 75
wait: 40
</setup action>
<target action>
face user: target
ZOOM: 200%, 75
CAMERA FOCUS: target, center, 30
MOTION WALK: user
move user: target, front, 30
face user: target
wait for movement
face user: target
motion attack: user
wait: 1
if $gameActors.actor(2).isStateAffected(44) || $gameActors.actor(2).isStateAffected(16)
animation 469: target
else if $gameActors.actor(2).isStateAffected(45) || $gameActors.actor(2).isStateAffected(17)
animation 470: target
else if $gameActors.actor(2).isStateAffected(46) || $gameActors.actor(2).isStateAffected(18)
animation 471: target
else if $gameActors.actor(2).isStateAffected(47) || $gameActors.actor(2).isStateAffected(19)
animation 472: target
else if $gameActors.actor(2).isStateAffected(48) || $gameActors.actor(2).isStateAffected(20)
animation 473: target
else if $gameActors.actor(2).isStateAffected(49) || $gameActors.actor(2).isStateAffected(21)
animation 474: target
else
action animation: target
end
wait for animation
action effect
face user: target
wait: 10
</target action>
<finish action>
move user: home
wait for movement
face user: forward
reset camera
reset zoom
wait for zoom
show battle hud
</finish action>

posts.author: Robro33
posts.body:
VinegarDude said:
i see, so to do multiple conditions do i gotta add || per condition?
Click to expand...
Yanfly's AS system isnt JS, but certain commands read JS - like IFs. logical operations like OR (||) and AND (&&) can be used in them.
a restriction to keep in mind is that you cant nest IFs without a separate plugin.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
If I'm not mistaken, you might not be able to check for the knockout state, since that state basically removes the enemy.
What you can do is what yanfly recommends: Put
Code:
Immortal: targets, true
somewhere at the start of your sequence. With this the enemy will not die, even when at 0 HP.
You condition can then just check for the 0 hp instead of the death state and you can just use
Code:
Immortal: targets, false
whenever you want the enemy to then die. (Like somewhere in that condition)
I don't remember if a. and b. actually worked in action sequencing, so if my suggestion doesn't work, you can then try and use
Code:
target.isStateAffected(x)
instead and see if that helps.
Robro33 said:
if your skills hit once, you can just check if the target's hp hit 0. targets arent killed immediately with yanfly's battle core is active, so you cant directly check if they died mid skill
Click to expand...
That is incorrect. They will die the moment their HP hits zero, and depending on whether or not you used the death break command, the sequence will just keep flailing on the corpse. You have to use immortal targets as described above.
Edit: Not quite incorrect. Apparently there is a default setup action that automatically turns enemies immortal, so if you don't have your own <setup action> in your sequence, enemies are actually immortal automatically.

yeah, i avoided mentioning checking for the death state (state 1 btw, not 0) because the default setup action makes targets immortal and immune to it. It slipped my mind that you could just turn it off though, so you could use the command SGHarlekin shared to turn it off or make a setup effect that doesnt make the targets immortal and then check if they have state 1 at some point afterwards once the damage is done.
that being said, a battler loses all of their states when they die without additional plugins, so checking for state 1 AND state 11 shouldnt be able to give you a true result.

alright, after reading all of this and messing with the action sequence plenty i ended with something like this:
<setup action>
display action
immortal: targets, true
camera clamp on
camera focus: target, center, 5
camera offset: down, 48
zoom: 110%, 5
</setup action>
<target action>
opacity not focus: 10%, 5
animation 42: target
animation 43: target
zoom: 120%, 5
wait: 20
zoom: 130%, 5
wait: 32
zoom: 140%, 5
wait: 32
zoom: 150%, 5
wait: 20
shake screen: 20, 23, 10
if target.isStateAffected(12)
action effect: target
reset camera: 5
reset zoom: 5
if target.hp === 0
immortal: targets, false
wait: 32
animation 902: target
wait: 32
shake screen: 6, 23, 10
wait for animation
animation 220: character 1
animation 220: character 3
wait for animation
else
action effect: target
reset camera: 5
reset zoom: 5
end
wait for animation
opacity not focus: 100%, 5
</target action>
<finish action>
clear battle log
</finish action>

the script call list is pinned in this section and is a large list of calls you can use anywhere JS is allowed. theres examples of them being used, but these are all stuff thats in the base engine.
since youre using them in conjunction with yanfly's plugins, theres some yanfly specific stuff that wouldnt be there and may be relevant to what youre doing though. like, yanfly notetags generally provide
user
and
target
references that you can use in place of
battler
,

,
